title: Building Lumenhold with AI: free-placement tower defense, and what phone testing changed
author: Affectionate-Mud-403
selftext:
I'm building Lumenhold, an incremental tower-defense game for Android and Windows. You arrange hexagonal strongholds and walls without a grid, shape enemy routes, and develop individual towers through research, cards and evolutions. I wanted run currency to stay useful even after permanent progression.



I'm directing the design and playtesting, with extensive AI assistance for implementation, debugging, design discussions and UI mockups. This post was also prepared with AI assistance. One concrete part of the workflow has been playing on my Galaxy Z Fold 5, reporting what feels confusing or slow, then iterating on specific problems.



That testing has mattered more than adding features. Menus that seemed fine on desktop became crowded on a phone; folding the screen exposed camera and sizing problems. Busy waves also revealed performance issues, so we've been working on route reuse, fewer repeated lookups and less frequent UI updates. Those changes still need real-device feedback rather than assuming a passing desktop test means the phone experience is fixed.



Another lesson came from watching a non-gamer: permanent upgrades and in-battle Gold upgrades were easy to confuse. We're adding clearer explanations and shortcuts between the related menus.



I'd be interested in how others keep AI-assisted projects manageable as systems accumulate, and how you decide when to stop adding features and focus on the first ten minutes.



The beta is playable on Android and Windows. If you'd like to test the controls, onboarding or performance, comment or message me. Android access currently requires adding your Google Play account to the closed test; send that email privately, not in a public comment. Windows access is a private download. No iPhone build yet, and no purchase is needed to try the beta.

comments.author: WWEtrump
comments.body: watching a non-gamer get confused is the best playtest, humbling every time. do you make your agent stop for your approval before changes land in the build? that saved me a ton when systems started piling up
